benchmark: CIS HPE Aruba Networking CX Switch Benchmark v1.0.1, Level 1
source: Control numbers from the public Tenable audit file CIS_HPE_Aruba_Networking_CX_Switch_v1.0.1_L1 (28 items). Wording is ours; the CIS text is not reproduced.

controls.ask: A separate local user group for security staff, allowed to read logs and little else, so nobody needs an admin account to audit.
Passwords and shared secrets are typed at the masked prompt, never inline on the command line where history and the screen keep them.
A password complexity policy: minimum length, a character from each class, and a history so old passwords do not come back.
The export password is your own, not the factory default, so secrets exported from this switch do not decrypt on any other CX switch.
The built-in admin account has a strong password.
Where the built-in groups do not fit, custom user groups allow only the commands listed in them.
CLI sessions are limited per user, close after 15 minutes idle, and login history is kept.
Telnet stays off on every VRF, which is the default. Remote CLI is SSH only.
The SSH allow-list is on, so only the management hosts or subnets listed can even try to log in.
SSH ciphers, MACs and key exchange are pinned to the list your policy approves instead of the defaults.
fix: ssh ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com aes128-gcm@openssh.com aes256-ctr aes128-ctr
ssh macs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com hmac-sha2-512 hmac-sha2-256

controls.ask: The SSH host key is regenerated with a strong type: ECDSA nistp256, ed25519, or RSA of 2048 bits.
NTP is authenticated with a shared key, so the switch only believes time servers that hold it.
The clock and time zone are set and NTP runs against more than one server.
No SNMP community is public or private, communities are read-only unless write is needed, and an access list limits who may ask.
The switch's own role-based rules decide which commands each user may run.
fix: aaa authorization commands ssh group local
aaa authorization commands console group local

controls.ask: Accounting is also kept on the switch, so the record of who did what survives the AAA server being down.
fix: aaa accounting all-mgmt default start-stop local

controls.ask: Only HPE-signed firmware loads. The switch checks the signature at download and at every boot.
Files move to and from the switch with SCP or SFTP, never TFTP.
The web UI and REST API are only on in the VRFs someone manages the switch from.
Web sessions time out as soon as operations allow; five minutes when only people use the web UI.
ServiceOS asks for a password at the console. Out of the box anyone at the console gets in as admin with none.
A banner before login says the switch is for authorized use only.
fix: Authorized use only. Activity on this switch is logged.

controls.ask: A scheduled job copies the running config off the switch regularly, over SFTP or SCP.
The hostname is unique and says where the switch is.
Factory reset from the front panel button stays off, which is the default, so physical access is not a wipe.
Every port nothing is plugged into is shut down.
Access ports facing end devices run BPDU guard: a switch plugged in shuts the port.
Ports that should never lead toward the root bridge run root guard.
